data.body:
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and it is NOT the comment cap. The bridge is duplicating comments into Jira every hour.

The 5000-comment cap is a **consequence**, not the cause. The cause is that the outbound
comment differ never recognises already-synced comments as present, so it **re-posts the same
comments to Jira on every hourly pass**. REB-1861 is simply the first issue to fill up.

### The decisive evidence

REB-1861 maps to local ticket `5200-e04e-246e-4aae` (`nonmystic-topiary-toadfish`) — a **closed**
story with **40 local comments**. Jira holds **5000**. A 125x divergence that no legitimate
activity explains.

Then the discriminating test: compare per-issue pending/applied comment counts between the
07:35Z run and the 17:33Z run — **ten passes apart, on closed tickets with no new local
comments.** If the sync converged, these would be zero after the first pass.

| Jira key | local ticket | status | local comments | pending 07:35 | pending 17:33 | applied 07:35 | applied 17:33 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REB-1580 | adroit-deductible-kakapo | closed | 24 | 21 | 21 | **21** | **21** |
| REB-1570 | fireless-schematic-gadwall | closed | 25 | 8 | 8 | **8** | **8** |
| REB-424 | orb-mantle-talon | closed | 25 | 3 | 3 | **3** | **3** |
| REB-1861 | nonmystic-topiary-toadfish | closed | 40 | 39 | 39 | 7 then 0 (cap) | 0 (cap) |

The counts are **identical ten hours later**, and `comments_applied` equals `pending` — so those
comments **successfully land in Jira on every single pass and are posted again the next hour**.
This is not a stalled queue; it is an active duplication loop. The differ decides a comment
"needs adding" when its body is not found in Jira, and for these comments that test never
becomes true even immediately after a successful post.

### Scale of the ongoing corruption

From the 17:33Z pass alone:

- **205 comments re-posted into Jira in one pass**, across **28 issues**.
- At the hourly cadence that is **~4,920 duplicate Jira comments per day**.
- REB-1861 re-emits 39/pass; 5000 / 39 ~= 128 passes ~= 5.3 days of hourly running to fill the cap
  — consistent with it tipping over on 2026-08-20.
- Top re-emitters right now: REB-1861 (39), REB-1580 (21), REB-1829 (18), REB-3067 (15),
  REB-2823 (15), REB-2882 (13), REB-1563 (13), REB-2213 (12).

**This is progressive and will keep claiming issues.** REB-1580 at 21/pass reaches the 5000 cap
in roughly ten days, then it too reds the bridge. Fixing only the cap-error classification would
silence the alarm while leaving the duplication running.

### Correction to my earlier comments

My first two comments correctly traced the *failure* path (cap refusal ->
`comment_errors` + silent-no-op canary -> `mutation_failures` -> exit 1) and that analysis stands
as the mechanism by which the red run is produced. But the *originating* defect is upstream of
all of it: comment-sync idempotency is broken. A guard for the per-issue count cap remains a
legitimate hardening item, but it is **not** the fix for this incident.

### Answer to "repo code or environment"

**Repo code.** Nothing about credentials, the runner, acli, or the workflow is at fault — 205
comments authenticate and post successfully every pass. The defect is in rebar's outbound
comment-diff / comment-id-recording path, which fails to mark landed comments as landed.

### Scope

This is materially larger than the filed bug (a red workflow) and involves ongoing writes to
production Jira. Escalating to the operator before any code change: the duplication loop, not
the cap, is what needs fixing, and stopping the bleed may warrant pausing the bridge first.
